## Question

What is the equal charge on the \( C_3 \)?

## Answer choices

- A: A: 2.5\ \mu\mathrm{C}

- B: B: 15\ \mu\mathrm{C}

- C: C: 55\ \mu\mathrm{C}

- D: D: 16\ \mu\mathrm{C}

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image depicts an electrical circuit diagram consisting of a battery and capacitors. 

- **Battery:** The circuit contains a 9-volt battery, represented by a rectangle with the positive (+) and negative (-) terminals labeled.
  
- **Capacitors:** There are three capacitors in the circuit.
  - \( C_1 \): A 4 microfarad (\( \mu \)F) capacitor.
  - \( C_2 \): A 12 microfarad (\( \mu \)F) capacitor.
  - \( C_3 \): A 2 microfarad (\( \mu \)F) capacitor.

- **Connections:**
  - \( C_1 \) and \( C_2 \) are connected in parallel to each other.
  - \( C_3 \) is connected in series with the parallel combination of \( C_1 \) and \( C_2 \).
  - The positive terminal of the battery is connected to \( C_1 \), and the circuit loops back to the negative terminal through \( C_3 \).

This setup creates a mixed series and parallel capacitor circuit connected to a 9 V power source.
